subject: Hierarchy of data set and density

messages.author: 5baa09ab3ebac9af
messages.subject: Hierarchy of data set and density
parts:
Hello List,

I was doing some search in the list serv, and found some information related
to my question; I have already post-stratified by treatment. However, I am
not quite sure if the setting I have is interfering with the density
estimates.

I am working with multiple bird species sampled at 20 point-transects with
unlimited distance, and the points were randomly selected using a grid
sampling approach.; 9 of these are in a treated area, and 11 in a reference
area. All the points but #. 20, have the same survey effort. The way I have
arranged the data in Distance is below:

*Two regions*: Treatment and Reference; I added a new field under region to
break each the *treatment* and the *reference *in 3 zones (Upper, Middle,
Low; this is RU (Reference Upper), RM, RL and so on for T) and I've assigned
area (ha) to each of the latter.

*Point count*, each has its label and survey effort

*Observation*: I have the label, radial distance, and a field for species.

In CDS I calculated the DF at the global level, and the density, the cluster
size, and the encounter rate post-stratifying by treatment, and then per
treatment per point (sample) to obtain individual density per point, but I
saw weird values (N<D) and would like to ask for some advice. I am also
getting some errors for the encounter rate.

I also ran the MCDS and calculated the detection function at the global
level. I did calculate density at the global level (mean_ weighted by total
effort per strata); also at the stratum (treatment) and Sample
(point-transect). It yielded awkward results specially when summarizing
data per point (sample), again N<D, and what seems to me high density
values. I got this error, which in my case might be causing problems:

forrtl: error (74): floating underflow
forrtl: error (74): floating underflow
forrtl: info (300): 24 floating underflow traps

Any insight would be appreciated. Thanks in advance;

Carolina
